headline: Council set a December 7 hearing on dog registration fee changes and directed staff to write a letter supporting EV fast chargers at City Hall.
summary: A consent agenda of warrants, resolutions, and a commission appointment passed 4-0. Officials heard updates on the Equitable Housing Needs Assessment, a CCRPC annual report, and department goals. A possible ordinance banning data centers was discussed, and the group agreed the issue needs to be addressed.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including warrants, resolutions, and a Finance Commission appointment, 4-0.
Directed staff to provide a letter of support to Gridwealth EV, LLC for Level 3 EV fast chargers at City Hall, 4-0.
Introduced amendments to Chapter 28 fees and set a public hearing for December 7, 2026, 4-0.

decision_evidence.quote: Motion to approve the consent agenda made by Councilor Turkos and seconded by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf. Motion passed 4-0.

A motion to direct staff to provide a letter of support to Gridwealth EV, LLC for their project proposal for the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure program to install Level 3 EV charging stations at City Hall made by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf and seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion passed 4-0.

A motion to introduce the amendments to Chapter 28 fees as presented and set a public hearing date for December 7, 2026, made by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf and seconded by Councilor Turkos. Motion passed 4-0.

VI. Council Reports 
Mayor Thomas Renner: Thank you to Councilor Goodrich and Deputy Mayor Oakleaf for covering my 
meetings while I was out of the state and I appreciate that. A huge thank you, and just to further what 
Councilor Turkos said to everybody who volunteered throughout the entire process of carving 
pumpkins. Especially to City staff and Downtown Winooski staff, we couldn’t do this without the 
community volunteers, but we really couldn’t do this without the city staff who coordinate so much in 
making that happen and receive way more pumpkins than you thought you were going to. It’s so 
beautiful seeing so many folks get together to make our tradition happen. Thank you very much. Just a 
reminder that tomorrow is voting day, so please make sure that you show up to vote if you haven’t   
already brought your ballot to City Hall. Voting is from 7 AM to 7 PM. And it is as every year; it is so 
crucial that we all show up to vote. We’re able to do it in Vermont and in Winooski, it is much easier 
than in other states even, let alone countries. Take advantage of that opportunity that not everybody 
gets to have and come on down to the Senior Center and cast your vote. 
 
Deputy Mayor Oakleaf: The Housing Commission met on Tuesday, and I stood in for the Mayor at the 
Planning Commission meeting on Thursday the 29th. At both meetings we had presentations on the 
Equitable Housing Needs Assessment, which is also on our agenda tonight. During the Housing 
Commission we elected officers and then talked about scheduling for our next two meetings. We will 
likely move up our December meeting probably a week but final dates for that will be confirmed and 
announced through our regular city channels. Safe, Healthy, Connected People Commission will also 
meet on November 10th.  
 
Councilor Al Turkos: The October 26th Inclusion and Belonging Commission meeting was canceled due 
to a lack of quorum and we’re in the process of rescheduling that meeting. The next Airport 
Commission meeting is this Wednesday, November 4th at 4 PM, and our next Downtown Winooski 
board meeting is on November 18th and we’re hoping to do that in-person at the new hotel. I just 
wanted to give a shout out as we had an incredible amount of volunteers and Winooski community 
members who showed up on Saturday morning to help us set up pumpkins and I just really wanted to, 
as it was early, and folks just really showed up and I want to express my gratitude as I expected to be 
there until 2 PM and we did so swiftly and I just really wanted to express my gratitude. 
 
Councilor Elsie Goodrich: I attended the Chittenden County Regional Housing Committee on October 
29th, where the Department of Housing and Community Development presented an update on the 802 
homes initiative, followed by the appearance from the Vermont League of Cities and Towns on the 
Community Housing Incentive Program or CHIP, and a roundtable discussion from the municipalities 
present on the work they are doing and the challenges they are facing. The Finance Commission will 
next meet on Tuesday, November 10th. We also interviewed a new member who was appointed tonight. 
Thank you to Natalie Alger, who will be a great addition. 
 
Councilor Eli Ogilvie: The Municipal Infrastructure Commission met on Thursday, October 29th. We 
continued our discussions regarding the best way to improve commission structure. For example, we 
discussed the possibility of combining commissions and which commissions would be the most 
compatible. For more details about the meeting, you can find the minutes on the Winooski website.

VII. City Updates 
 
Elaine Wang, City Manager, gave the following updates: 
The General Election is tomorrow! Please bring your voted ballot to the Winooski Senior Center at 123 Barlow 
Street from 7 AM to 7 PM. If you need help with your ballot or voter registration, please see an election worker 
at the Senior Center. Remember – you can view your voter registration information and ballot status at 
vote.vermont.gov. 
The Safe, Healthy, Connected People Commission is looking for new members. This commission advises the 
City Council on the City’s Strategic Vision to foster relationships across generations and cultures by providing a 
safe and healthy environment and providing opportunities to connect and engage. They discuss programs, 
events, and policies that relate to the library, senior center, recreation and parks, as well as topics related to 
our police, fire, and code enforcement services. Meetings are held at 5:30 PM every 2nd Tuesday at Winooski 
City Hall with an online option. Residents with relevant experience, skills, interests, or a willingness to engage 
are encouraged to apply for this opportunity and participate in local government. The City Council and staff 
welcome diverse voices, and if you've never served on a board, commission, or committee before, we'll do our 
best to support you! To learn more and apply, visit winooskivt.gov/SHCP. 
 
In case you missed it: the Winooski Police Department has temporarily relocated from Winooski City Hall at 27 
West Allen Street to the Champlain Mill Building at 20 Winooski Falls Way to begin the police department 
renovation process. To learn more about how to access the Winooski Police Department, please visit the news 
updates section at winooskivt.gov/police. 
 
And finally, we celebrated another incredible Halloween in Winooski event over the weekend. I'd like to 
personally thank our Community Services Department team, Downtown Winooski, the Department of Public 
Works, all the event sponsors, and to the great many community volunteers who came together to make it a 
huge success. 
VIII. Regular Items 
A. Discussion: Equitable Housing Needs Assessment Presentation - Jazmine Hurley, Housing Initiative 
Director, Michael Moser, UVM CRS 
 
Minutes: Michael Moser gave an overview about the Equitable Housing Needs Assessment and 
highlighted four specific components: A literature review, resource guide, community engagement, and 
a final report draft. Sixty-two percent of households rent in Winooski, which is more than twice the 
statewide rate and stated that “Winooski is like no place in Vermont”. Focus groups worked with 
“trusted voices” in the community to hear their needs and guide the city on their housing goals. The 
final report should be available soon and asked for input on behalf of Council for additional information 
they could add to the report. 
 
The Council had many questions related to parking in the city, barriers to public transportation, types of 
housing needed for the community, continued engagement opportunities, and landlord 
acknowledgements. They all shared their appreciation of efforts with the report and involving the 
community throughout this process.  
 
B. Discussion: Chittenden County Regional Planning Commission (CCRPC) Annual Report Presentation 
and Budget Review - Elaine Wang, City Manager, and Charlie Baker, Executive Director

Minutes: Taylor Newton, the Deputy Director of CCRPC, spoke on behalf of the Executive Director and 
gave a comprehensive overview of the support their organization assists with for the city. This annual 
report outlined the scope of practice the planning commission does with all municipalities and 
highlighted some of the work specifically in Winooski related to brownfield assistance, review of major 
construction projects, and other available services they can provide in the new fiscal year (e.g., traffic 
calming studies). 
 
The mayor mentioned their excitement over future traffic calming studies and thanked them for their 
presentation. Deputy Mayor Oakleaf asked further questions related to transportation services and 
Michael O’Brien, who is a Winooski representative, shared their knowledge as well. The City Manager 
also gave comments that the Community Equity Policy Advisor is also a part of the services CCRPC 
helps with.  
 
C. Discussion/Approval: Letter of Support for Electric Vehicle Fast Chargers at City Hall to Be Installed, 
Owned, and Operated by Private Company - Ravi Venkataraman, Director of City Planning 
 
Minutes: The Director of City Planning gave a high-level overview of goals and initial questions the 
Council had regarding installation of Level 3 Electric Vehicle Fast Chargers. Winooski is a priority 
location for EV readiness, and the presented letter of support is required on behalf of the city to 
continue the process with the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure program. After reviewing possible 
locations for these fast chargers, the city believes that City Hall would be the best location for installing 
these fast chargers with an overview of the review process shared by the Director of City Planning. 
 
Questions and discussion amongst the Council and staff ensued related to costs, specific directives, 
management of the chargers, and timeframe for completion. The city identified Gridwealth EV, LLC as a 
good provider to work with on this project, especially after discussing with other municipalities who 
shared their experience using their services. The infrastructure program would pay approximately 
eighty percent of the cost, while the city would be responsible for the other twenty percent. Because of 
the cost on behalf of the city, the private company would help to install, operate, and manage these 
chargers. 
 
Motion: A motion to direct staff to provide a letter of support to Gridwealth EV, LLC for their project 
proposal for the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure program to install Level 3 EV charging stations 
at City Hall made by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf and seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion passed 4-0. 
 
A recess was taken from 8:04 PM to 8:09 PM. 
 
D. Discussion: Goal Updates: Safe, Healthy, Connected People; Municipal Infrastructure; and Housing - 
Jazmine Hurley, Housing Initiative Director, Ray Coffey, Community Services Director, John Audy, Fire 
Chief, Justin Huizenga, Police Chief, and Jon Rauscher, Public Works Director 
 
Minutes: The Public Works Director started the discussion with an overview of first quarter work, and 
noted how proud he is of this team, and how productive the first quarter was within their scope of 
practice. Main Street is mostly completed, and the new parking garage and hotel project are near 
completion. Continued work with stormwater projects as well as phosphorus reduction and infiltration 
work is still on-going and the Public Works Director shared project projections for the second quarter. 
The mayor shared their appreciation with the Main Street project and councilors were able to ask 
additional questions related to line striping, bridge construction and traffic calming opportunities.

The Community Services Director gave a brief overview stating that they are off to a good start to the 
year, especially with the implementation and strong investment of the full-time Senior Center position 
and their programming. In addition, they spoke about the new Library location seeing an increase in 
new patrons, while needing further outreach from those that frequented the old location. 
 
The Fire Chief highlighted the addition of 111 Weaver St., and its plans for full utilization soon. The 
mayor gave comment regarding other municipalities reaching out to him and how impressed they are 
with being able to tackle housing for the Fire Department. 
 
The Police Chief spoke about the Police Department renovations Request for Procurement, as well as 
the move to the temporary location being up and running. He invited all to check out the new 
operations. 
 
The Housing Initiative Director gave an update on the Armory project as well as the Housing Trust Fund. 
 
E. Discussion/Approval: Introduction to Update Ordinance - Chapter 28 Fees - Angela Aldieri, Finance 
Director 
 
Minutes: The Finance Director spoke to Council on behalf of the City Clerk regarding the fee amount for 
dog registrations. Due to the City not having an established animal and rabies control program, the 
current fee structure needs to change based on Vermont statute (the registration fee would be 
reduced). A public hearing is required as the next step to move forward with the proposed ordinance 
and fee change. The mayor gave their appreciation from the Clerk for bringing this to their attention 
with no additional questions or feedback. 
 
Motion: A motion to introduce the amendments to Chapter 28 fees as presented and set a public 
hearing date for December 7, 2026, made by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf and seconded by Councilor Turkos. 
Motion passed 4-0. 
 
F. Discussion: Data Center Prohibition Ordinance - Mayor Thomas Renner 
 
Minutes: The mayor introduced a memo and appreciated a discussion amongst council regarding a 
possible ordinance change prohibiting data centers in Winooski. There is limited space within the city, 
and the mayor would like to ensure for the future an update to the ordinance. Discussion amongst the 
council ensued about possibly adding language to the Unified Land Use and Development Regulations 
and has also asked for the City’s legal council to review. There is an understanding that technology 
development is moving quickly and the council agreed that this needs to be addressed, especially 
ensuring that any possible language does not have any adverse consequences with current 
infrastructure already in place in Winooski. 
 
IX. Adjourn 
 
Motion: Motion to adjourn made by Councilor Turkos and seconded by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf. Motion 
passed 4-0 and the meeting adjourned at 8:47 PM.
